issues.legal_issue: A dispute over who is entitled to compensation may be referred to the court after the Collector has made and apportioned an award when the claimant’s title devolved after the award.
material_facts: The Collector made and filed awards apportioning compensation among the then-known claimants.
After the awards, a statutory change vested the former owner’s title in the State before possession of the acquired land was taken.
The State claimed the compensation as successor to that title, and the Collector referred the dispute over entitlement to the court.
issues.conclusion: The Collector could refer the dispute under Section 30 even though the award had already apportioned compensation. A person whose title devolved after the award could seek such a reference; the State had no claim under Section 18 as a person interested when the award was made, but could claim under Section 30 on the basis of its later-acquired title. Section 30 prescribes no period of limitation, and the Collector’s power to refer is discretionary.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 confer distinct powers applicable in different circumstances. A person identified in the award, or notified under Section 12(2), who rejects the award must seek a Section 18 reference within its prescribed period. Section 30 permits the Collector, after compensation is settled under Section 11, to refer a dispute about apportionment or the person entitled to payment, including a dispute arising because title devolved after the award; no limitation period is prescribed for that reference. The fact that the Collector apportioned compensation does not bar a Section 30 reference. The Court disapproved Boregowda v. Subbaramiah, AIR 1959 Mysore 265, and relied on Promotha Nath Mitra v. Rakhal Das Addy, 11 Cal. L.J. 420, concerning prosecution of a reference by a successor in title.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and compensation_awarded_and_apportioned and claimant_acquired_title_after_award and dispute_over_compensation_recipient

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns compensation for land acquired through a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.compensation_awarded_and_apportioned: The Collector made an award fixing compensation and allocating it among persons then known or believed to have an interest.
predicates.claimant_acquired_title_after_award: The claimant acquired the former owner’s title after the Collector made the award.
predicates.dispute_over_compensation_recipient: The claimant and another person assert conflicting rights to receive the compensation.
predicates.collector_may_refer_entitlement_dispute: The Collector may refer the dispute over who is entitled to the compensation to the court.

issues.definition: When compensation has been awarded and apportioned in a land-acquisition proceeding, a dispute may be referred if a claimant later acquires title and contests who should receive the compensation.

issues.legal_issue: An award fixing compensation does not itself create the right to compensation, and a transfer of the landowner’s title before possession may transfer the right to compensation to the successor.
material_facts: The Collector made the awards before the former owner’s title vested by statute in the State.
The title vested in the State before the Government took possession under the acquisition proceeding.
The State claimed the compensation as the successor to the former owner’s title.
issues.conclusion: The award was an offer and did not itself create the right to compensation. The former owner’s title to the land was extinguished when possession was taken, so the statutory transfer of title before possession caused the right to compensation to devolve upon the State.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11 and 12 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the award fixes and apportions the Government’s offer; it is not the source of the right to compensation. Section 16 provides for the land to vest absolutely in the Government on possession, while Section 48 permits withdrawal from acquisition before possession. Sections 28 and 34 support the significance of possession by providing for interest from the date possession is taken. The Court relied on Serju Prasad Sahu v. State of Uttar Pradesh, AIR 1965 SC 1763, for the proposition that the owner’s right is extinguished when the Government takes possession after an award is made.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns compensation for land acquired through a statutory land-acquisition proceeding.
predicates.compensation_award_made: The Collector made an award stating the compensation offered for the land.
predicates.title_transferred_before_possession: The former owner’s title was transferred to another person before the acquiring authority took possession of the land.
predicates.compensation_right_devolves_with_title: The right to claim compensation devolves with the title transferred before possession is taken.

issues.definition: If title to the land is transferred after an award but before possession, the compensation claim devolves with that title.

issues.legal_issue: The Collector’s allocation of compensation does not finally determine competing rights among claimants, and payment to the person named in the award does not bar another claimant from pursuing a claim against the recipient.
material_facts: The Collector apportioned compensation in the awards between the persons then known or believed to be interested in the land.
The State later asserted a competing claim to compensation based on title that had devolved to it after the awards.
The dispute concerned entitlement among claimants, rather than the Collector’s liability to pay the compensation awarded.
issues.conclusion: The apportionment is conclusive between the Collector and the persons interested, not among those persons. Payment to the person identified in the award discharges the State’s liability, subject to any court modification, but leaves a claimant free to pursue the entitlement dispute through a Section 30 reference or a separate suit.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12, 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 distinguish the Collector’s award and payment obligations from the final adjudication of competing claimants’ rights. The award is conclusive as between the Collector and persons interested, but the Collector does not finally adjudicate title to the compensation as between those persons. Section 31 payment to the person declared entitled by the award discharges the State’s liability, subject to court modification; the claimant may still assert a right to the money by a Section 30 reference or separate suit.

predicates.award_names_compensation_recipient: The Collector’s award identifies a person to whom compensation is to be paid.
predicates.another_claimant_asserts_competing_entit: A claimant other than the person named in the award asserts a competing right to the compensation.
predicates.award_allocation_not_final_between_claim: The award’s allocation does not finally determine the competing claimants’ rights against one another.

issues.definition: When an award names a compensation recipient and another claimant asserts entitlement, the allocation does not finally resolve their competing rights.
